Prevention: Early land preparation that includes clearing and burying/burning of weed remnants
Intercropping with legumes for complete ground cover to suppress the weeds.
Plant maize at 90 x 90cm, 3 plants per hill and plant legume seeds between maize stations
Without intercropping, plant maize at 75 x 25cm
Early planting with effective rains of at least 30 mm cumulative
Use of certified seed to avoid contamination
Clean farm implements to avoid spread
Use contour ridges to restrict movement of weed seed with water
If there is a history or the weed in the field treat with a pre emergence herbicide
Monitoring: Look for fleshy, broad leaved plants with dark green alternate leaves and lilac/ blue flowers
Scout the fields weekly looking for emerging weeds
Consider direct control before the weeds flower
Direct Control (Non-chemical): Uproot as soon as weeds appear, remove from the field and bury 30cm deep
Hand hoeing as soon as weeds emerge - this should only be carried out when the weather is dry and avoid breaking up/cutting the plant as this can spread the weed.
Remove plants from the field and bury/burn
Hoeing can cause the weed to fragment - take care to remove all plant parts
Uprooting and hand hoeing before weeds set seed
Direct Control (Chemical): Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
If there is a history of the weed use
Acetochlor (Acetochlor 900EC, Sprint 900EC) it is a pre-emergence herbicide.
Apply at a rate of 7.5 ml in a 15 litre tank immediately after sowing
SC) is a post-emergence herbicide applied once the weed has germinated and before maize is sown.
Use at a rate of 23 ml in a 15 litre tank
